songInfo.title: Where the Streets Have No Name

scalesUsed.notes: D - E - F# - G - A - B - C# - D
scalesUsed.application: Shapes the soaring, euphoric melody and the arpeggiated chime triads that define the song's signature atmosphere

scalesUsed.notes: D - E - F# - G - A - B - C - D
scalesUsed.application: Introduced dramatically in the bridge when the song pivots to the flattened 7th degree (C major chord)
Provides clean, uplifting melodic phrases and upper-register guitar swells

keyAndScale.keySignature: Two sharps (F#, C#) for D major, with an occasional accidental C natural in the bridge
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: B minor (featured prominently in the chorus progression)

mainProgression.description: An uplifting, anthemic arena-rock progression. The Edge maintains the open D string (or high D note) across chord shifts, providing an unbroken shimmering anchor as the harmonies move underneath.

sectionProgressions.description: Continuous straight eighth-note triad arpeggios that interlock with dotted-eighth digital delay to produce a galloping sixteenth-note wall of chime

sectionProgressions.progression: D - D - G - G - D - D - A - A
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: I - I - IV - IV - I - I - V - V
sectionProgressions.description: Expansive diatonic changes propelled by driving bass pulses and chiming treble guitar textures

sectionProgressions.progression: G - D - Bm - A - G - D
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: IV - I - vi - V - IV - I
sectionProgressions.description: Emotional climax introducing the relative minor (Bm) before cascading triumphantly back to the tonic D

sectionProgressions.progression: C - C - G - G - D - D
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: bVII - bVII - IV - IV - I - I
sectionProgressions.description: A dramatic modal shift to C major (bVII) that injects raw rock tension and urgency before resolving to D

harmonicFunction: D (I) - Tonic chord delivering an open, spiritual sense of resolution and light
G/D (IV/I) - Subdominant chord retaining the D pedal note for seamless modal continuity
Bm (vi) - Relative minor providing momentary melancholy within an otherwise triumphant landscape
A (V) - Dominant major building forward momentum into subsequent sections
C (bVII) - Flattened seventh in the bridge providing powerful Mixolydian release

techniques.name: Dotted-Eighth Rhythmic Delay Sync
techniques.description: The Edge's definitive sonic signature. Playing straight eighth notes with a digital delay set strictly to a dotted eighth note (3/16 note, or 357 ms at 126 BPM) so that the echoes interlock perfectly between the picked notes, generating a driving sixteenth-note gallop

notes: Set delay time strictly to 357 ms (or sync to 126 BPM tempo clock via tap tempo)
Set delay feedback to 2-3 audible repeats and mix level to roughly 65-70%
Pick straight, steady eighth notes without syncopating your pick hand
Hold the pick with the textured grip edge striking the string for the iconic Herdim chiming scrape
Keep every note cleanly articulated on strings 1, 2, and 3
sequence: Form the D major triad at fret 10/11 on strings 1, 2, and 3
Pick straight down-up eighth notes: string 3, string 2, string 1, string 2
Listen to how the delay repeats fill in the spaces to create a galloping train effect
Shift middle and pinky fingers to fret 12 for the G/D chord while maintaining the identical picking rhythm
tips: Do not try to play sixteenth notes with your pick; let the delay do the work
Timing accuracy is paramount: if you drift off tempo, the echoes will clash into rhythmic mud
Use the bridge and middle pickup position on a Stratocaster into a slightly driven Vox AC30

techniques.name: Open-String Drone Chording
techniques.description: Voicing upper-register triads while allowing the open D (4th string) or high E string to ring continuously, creating an ambient harmonic halo across chord changes

notes: Let the open 4th string (D) drone beneath shifting chord shapes
Avoid muting adjacent strings with fret-hand fingertips
Use light pick attack to prevent over-driving the input of the delay processor
Roll back guitar volume slightly to clean up lower-mid frequencies
sequence: Strike open D string firmly on beat 1
Finger upper triad shapes at frets 7, 9, and 10
Allow the resonance of the open string to bridge the gap between chord finger shifts
tips: Keep your fret-hand fingers arched high on their tips
Use a compressor pedal before the delay to even out the attack of picked and open strings

sections.name: Ambient Organ & Chime Intro
sections.description: Brian Eno's warm church-organ synthesizer chords wash over the track before The Edge's chiming Stratocaster guitar quietly emerges from the mist with dotted-eighth echoes.
notes: Play gentle single-note swells as the synthesizer chords build
Let the delay repeats blend into the ambient synthesizer bed
Gradually roll up your guitar volume knob from 4 to 8
Prepare pick hand for the rhythmic entrance on beat 1

sections.name: Galloping 3/16 Delay Arpeggio Entrance
sections.description: Larry Mullen Jr.'s hi-hat counts in, and the iconic galloping guitar riff bursts through the mix with crystalline clarity, driving the track forward with unstoppable momentum.
notes: Pick steady straight eighth notes; do not rush or drag against the tempo
Ensure string 1 (10th fret) rings clearly against strings 2 and 3
Let the 357 ms delay repeats create the galloping sixteenth-note pattern
Keep pick depth shallow so the plectrum glides across the strings

sections.name: Verse Driving Rhythm & Drone Strings
sections.description: Bono delivers the iconic lyrics over a locked-in rhythm section. The Edge shifts between upper-register arpeggios and full open-voiced chords with ringing delay trails.
sections.progression: D - D - G - G - D - D - A - A
notes: Maintain unwavering pick-hand eighth-note pulse
Transition smoothly to open G chord voicings at fret 3
Let the delay tails bridge the gap during chord changes
Support the vocal narrative without overpowering the lyrical space

sections.name: Chorus Stadium Ascent
sections.description: The song expands into a massive stadium anthem. The progression steps through G, D, Bm, and A as ringing open chords wash over the drums.
sections.progression: G - D - Bm - A - G - D
notes: Dig in with firmer pick attack for stadium-sized dynamic projection
Voice the Bm chord cleanly across strings 5 through 1
Let every chord ring for its full duration before chopping into the next
Feel the emotional release as the harmony returns to D

sections.name: Bridge Modal Shift (bVII C Major Lift)
sections.description: The harmonic landscape pivots unexpectedly to C major (bVII). The flattened seventh introduces raw urgency and gritty rock bite before returning to G and D.
notes: Emphasize the low C root note on the 5th string (fret 3)
Strum with aggressive syncopation to highlight the dramatic modal shift
Feel the transition from heavenly D major to earthbound C Mixolydian
Build dynamic volume to maximum intensity before the final chorus

sections.name: Outro Climax & Fading Echo Cascades
sections.description: The signature galloping arpeggio returns at peak intensity before slowly disintegrating into lingering delay repeats and organ pads as the track fades.
notes: Resume high-register triad picking on strings 1, 2, and 3
Gradually reduce pick velocity to facilitate a smooth, natural fade
Allow the delay repeats to oscillate naturally into the room sound
Conclude with a single ringing D major harmonic at fret 12

guitar.recommended: 1976 Fender Stratocaster (Black finish, maple neck, pickup position 2: bridge + middle)
guitar.pickup: Bridge and middle single-coils combined (Position 2 / in-between) for maximum glass and quack

amp.recommended: 1964 Vox AC30 Top Boost combo with Celestion Alnico Blue speakers
alternatives: Fender 65 Deluxe Reverb with treble boost

effects.distortion: Preamp overdrive from Korg SDD-3000 rack unit pushing the front of the Vox AC30
effects.other: Digital delay set to dotted eighth (357 ms, 3 repeats, 65% mix), dimpled nylon pick (Herdim)

beginner.title: Learning the D Major Triad Shapes
steps: Master the D major triad at frets 10 and 11 on strings 1, 2, and 3
Learn the G/D chord shape at fret 12 and practice switching between them
Practice picking straight eighth notes evenly without rushing
beginner.goals: Play the fundamental chord shapes smoothly with steady pick-hand timing

intermediate.title: Dialing In Dotted-Eighth Delay
steps: Set your delay pedal to 357 ms (or use tap tempo synced to 126 BPM)
Lock straight eighth-note picking against the sixteenth-note delay feedback
Play through the verse and chorus chord progressions with continuous delay
intermediate.goals: Execute the signature galloping delay rhythm with flawless tempo synchronization

advanced.title: Pick Dynamics & Tone Sculpting
steps: Use a textured nylon pick (Herdim style) striking with the gripped edge for chime
Balance guitar volume knob adjustments to manage amplifier saturation
Perform the complete 5:37 album arrangement with studio-accurate dynamics and touch
advanced.goals: Master The Edge's signature arena-rock sound, timing precision, and ambient control

commonMistakes: Trying to pick sixteenth notes instead of playing steady eighth notes and letting the delay create the gallop
Setting delay tempo incorrectly; even a 5 ms error will cause the repeats to clash violently with the beat
Picking with too heavy a touch, which causes the delay repeats to distort and lose their sparkling chime
Failing to mute unplayed lower strings, allowing muddy rumble to overtake the shimmering delay lines
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Steady eighth-note alternate picking drill on a single string with a metronome at 126 BPM
10 mins: Slow delay calibration: play 1 beat of eighth notes, pause, and verify repeats fall on 16ths
10 mins: D and G/D triad arpeggio transition work at frets 10-12
10 mins: Full playthrough of verse, chorus, and bridge transitions with backing track
focusAreas: Exact millisecond or tap-tempo delay synchronization
Consistent pick attack velocity across strings 3, 2, and 1
Clean transition between high-register arpeggios and full open-chord strumming
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 126 BPM and play straight eighth notes without delay to verify your internal clock
Engage delay with 1 repeat; ensure each delay echo lands exactly between the metronome clicks
Increase delay repeats to 3 and practice maintaining strict eighth-note attack for 5 minutes continuously
